//: LibreLane 3.0.0.dev44 config for a LOCAL hardening run of this tile.
This is NOT the Tiny Tapeout submission config. src/config.json is, and it
is the template default that TinyTapeout/tt-gds-action merges with its own
shuttle settings (die area from the tiles field, the tile power grid, the
harness pin placement). This file exists so the same tool at the same
version can be run here to answer one question: does this design actually
place, route, and pass DRC and LVS on the real IHP PDK?
Run it with: make harden. Paths are dir:: relative to the repo root,
which is passed as --design-dir, because LibreLane refuses to read outside
the design directory and ../src would escape it.
Real constraints, not the generic fallback. Without these two keys
LibreLane warns and substitutes an SDC of its own, and any slack number
quoted from that is not worth having.
The die is Tiny Tapeout's real 1x1 tile for this shuttle, taken from their
own floorplan template tt/tech/ihp-sg13g2/def/tt_block_1x1_pgvdd.def:
Not the 167 x 108 um the template's info.yaml comment quotes, which is off
by 74% and is what an earlier version of this file believed. Fixing the die
rather than letting the floorplanner choose is the point: it makes the run
answer 'does it fit the tile I claimed' instead of 'what area does it want'.
scripts/harden.sh takes HARDEN_DIE="W H" to override it, which is how the
1x2 comparison in docs/design.md was run.
Placement density target, the same value src/config.json uses. Both numbers
below the one here were measured, not guessed:
60  the LibreLane and template default. Global placement stops with
[GPL-0302] at 64.2% core utilisation and suggests 0.65.
80  places, but detailed placement fails after clock tree synthesis with
[DPL-0036], unable to legalise 10 instances once 234 hold buffers
have been inserted.
85  places, routes and signs off clean.
Post route the design is 82.7% of the tile, so the placer has to be told to
expect a dense result. HARDEN_DENSITY overrides it.
Margins, mirroring src/config.json.
On the one remaining design rule violation, the clock tree root buffer
driving 16 sinks against the library default_max_fanout of 8: two knobs
were tried and neither is here because neither did anything at all.
CTS_SINK_CLUSTERING_SIZE 40 (up from OpenROAD's default 20)
MAX_FANOUT_CONSTRAINT 8 plus CTS_BALANCE_LEVELS true
Both runs produced metrics identical to the baseline to four decimal
places, including the same 51 clock buffers and the same violation. Dead
settings are worse than no settings, so they are recorded here and not
applied. See docs/design.md section 7.
Hold margins from the template.
KLayout DRC and XOR are single threaded unless told otherwise, and the
maximal sg13g2 DRC runset can take longer than every other stage combined.
4 is a deliberately modest committed default because it has to be a fixed
number in JSON. scripts/harden.sh computes a better one from nproc and
overrides it, and honours KLAYOUT_THREADS if you set it. Raise this if you
have the machine to yourself; leave it low if several PnR runs share it,
since oversubscribing cores is slower than running single threaded.
Keep signoff on. DRC and LVS clean is the whole claim.
Do not buffer the outputs, as the tile drives the harness mux directly.
The ring oscillators in src/ring_osc.v are deliberate combinational
loops. Routing them in a small die is congested, so allow the global
router to exceed its congestion estimate, exactly as src/config.json does.
